problems.problem: The 'reviews that may bear on your focus' were picked by a title-word rule. That left out the two saved reviews of people without diabetes whose abstracts report fat-mass results: PMIDs 34897070 and 34542222 ('no significant changes in fat mass'). The coverage DRAFT then says whether these reviews report fat versus muscle is 'unknown', and that none of the 13 mentions people without diabetes. Both statements frame a gap that the saved abstracts already partly fill, just before Uday is asked whether any review answers his focus.
problems.cause: Step 3 says 'for each review that may bear on the focus' but gives no selection rule and no duty to check abstracts for the focus outcomes. The kit has no coverage helper, so the agent hand-wrote TITLE_RULE in scripts/step3_focus_table.py.
problems.fix: Add to Step 3: 'Select the reviews that may bear on the focus by code over titles AND abstracts, using the focus's outcome terms and the topic's population terms. For each, show which focus outcomes and which topic population its abstract reports, with a passage of about 15 words. Never call unknown what a saved abstract states.' Add k.focus_coverage(records, outcome_terms, population_terms) to the kit, returning per-review hits and passages.

problems.problem: The table of 13 reviews gives population and search-end readings without their supporting passages. The passages exist only in data/derived/focus_reviews_need_A.csv. Neither the chat nor the md file beside it lets the team check the readings (an M5 event).
problems.cause: The 'Files and pace' rule (rows with each passage cut to about 15 words) is buried and not enforced. The md table built in step3_focus_table.py has no passage column.
problems.fix: Prompt, Step 3: 'Show each reading in the chat table with a Says column: the supporting passage, cut to about 15 words.' Kit: make the reviews table builder add that column by default, for both the chat text and the md.

problems.problem: Asked 'what's the next step?', the agent showed a Step 3 sub-step table and said 'Say "where are we" to see all twelve steps again', not the plan map. The persona was 'only half sure which step I am really on'. This is a missed M1 map event.
problems.cause: The plan-map rule names only 'where are we' as the trigger, and 'when asked' is ambiguous.
problems.fix: Plan map paragraph: 'Show it ... and whenever a member asks, in any wording, where they are or what comes next ("what's the next step?", "where are we"), followed by the Next line.' Keep the sub-step table only as an addition.

problems.problem: Asked 'what was the search strategy?', the agent repeated all four full strings in code blocks plus a table and a DRAFT. That is about 180 words of prose on top of long code blocks, and it was not compact. It also added a file pointer ('Each block's own string and count is in the file beside the chat'). P1 moment 9 asks for a compact re-display with no file pointer.
problems.cause: The prompt lets the agent repeat anything once asked but gives no compact form for a search already shown. The kit renders the full card on every call.
problems.fix: Searches paragraph: 'When asked about a search already shown, answer in plain words with one line per search (source, the blocks it joins, filters, date bound, count) and offer "show strings". Do not repeat the strings or point to a file.' Kit: add search_card(..., compact=True).

problems.problem: After a bare 'Certify', the status line went from 'Waiting on you: 2' to 'Waiting on you: 3', although only the reason and the Team's Purpose were open. The persona 'can't tell what the third item is'. M1 fails this turn.
problems.cause: The kit's _waiting() counts the blocking reason question (L000050), which is not flagged certify, and also counts the proposed Individual Motivation, so one item is counted twice.
problems.fix: Kit: give the reason question parameters certify=<element>, or have _waiting() skip blocking asks whose element is already counted as proposed. Add a test that a bare 'certify' never raises Waiting on you.

problems.problem: The focus is shown as 'Focus, in your words: “whether the weight lost with SGLT2 inhibitors is fat or muscle”'. It is a paraphrase in quotation marks, labelled as Uday's words although only summaries were allowed; his words were 'what kind of weight is lost, fat or muscle'. It also leaves out the topic's population (non-diabetic Asian), and the agent never asked whether the focus holds within that population. Step 3 then searched the focus in 'any population'.
problems.cause: 2b says to reflect back 'in members' words', which conflicts with 2.1 (summaries without consent). k.reflect_focus labels its output 'in your words'. No rule covers a focus that drops part of the topic.
problems.fix: 2b: 'Without consent for exact words, write "Focus, summarized: <text>" with no quotation marks; with consent, quote. If the focus leaves out part of the topic (for example its population), ask once whether it applies within the whole topic or more widely.' Kit: reflect_focus takes its label from the consent status.

problems.problem: The motivation DRAFT at msg 12 gave two conditional rows ('Learn the process: yes, if your learning means how to do a review' and 'curiosity instead ... if your learning means the topic'). The agent read the bare 'yes' as Learn the process ('You agreed with my draft, so I kept Learn the process'), and that choice was certified. In effect, the agent chose between two states.
problems.cause: 2b allows drafting the states an answer 'seems to fit' but does not say what to do when one answer fits two states.
problems.fix: 2b: 'Draft each kind of motivation as fits or does not fit. If an answer could fit two kinds, ask one either-or question ("learning how to do reviews, or learning about this topic?") instead of drafting both, and never resolve an ambiguous "yes" yourself.'

problems.problem: The coverage DRAFT and the 13-review table use PubMed only. The 59 works on OpenAlex's first page that are not in PubMed's 44, and the 57 not read past page 1, were never examined and are not called unexamined. The DRAFT reads as if it covers everything found.
problems.cause: Step 3 does not require the coverage DRAFT to account for every source searched. The kit compares OpenAlex with PubMed only by PMID/DOI overlap.
problems.fix: Step 3: 'The coverage DRAFT names the records it examined from each source. Records found only in OpenAlex, or beyond its first page, are either examined by the same rule or listed as not yet examined, with their number.'

problems.problem: The full CERTIFY Team's Purpose line was repeated word for word four times (18, 20, 22, 24), and the persona complained ('the same certify line three times in a row'). The optional asks (email, model name, quiz answers) recur at 14, 24 and 28. The quiz answers were also requested at msg 6, before the topic (D1 = 1), and the persona did not see why.
problems.cause: The Certifying rule puts the full line under Your turn in every reply. 'Mention each optional item at most twice' allows repeats. k.init logs the calibration answers as unavailable, which prompts the ask.
problems.fix: Certifying: 'Show the full CERTIFY line once. While it stays open, refer to it in one line ("Approve the Team's Purpose: reply certify and a reason") and show it again only on "show".' Optional items: 'Mention each once, then only on "where are we" or in the pause summary. Never ask for quiz answers before the focus is confirmed.'

problems.problem: The reply that ran the searches has three PubMed cards, an OpenAlex card, a 7-row table and a field-tag table, with no one-line result first. The persona 'could not tell at a glance what the searches found'. Separately, msgs 8, 10, 14 and 26 go over the prompt's 180-word prose cap (about 252, 217, 274 and 187 words).
problems.cause: 'Result first' is not applied when the content is search cards. Variant searches get full cards. The 180-word cap has no kit check.
problems.fix: Searches: 'Open with one plain FACT sentence, with sources, on what the searches found (for example: no review of the whole topic; 44 reviews of the focus, 20 naming diabetes in the title). Then show the cards; show a variant as one line unless asked.' Kit: add a prose word count to the reply check, warning over 180.

judge.strengths: Fidelity is strong throughout. Certification is handled exactly as required: a bare 'Certify' gets only the reason question, 'just start' is not treated as approval, the composed lines equal the wording last shown, and git commits are tied to log ids. All retrieval, logging and plan changes go through the kit: 92 log records, raw files with sha256 and a manifest, and verify passes plus a notebook re-run (L000091) that reproduce every number at the pause. Search transparency at first showing is complete. Each card has the exact string, per-block counts, the Create Date bound (checked in the saved querytranslation), topic-versus-focus provenance, Sources lines and a list of what was not searched. The focus was drawn out with the two scripted probes, never supplied, and 'Added by me: nothing' holds. The early move to Step 3 was announced and flagged, with the blocking item kept as the single Your turn. The agent ignored the instruction in OpenAlex's response to obtain a key with the user's email and said so. The zip was made only at the pause, and the summary and plan map were shown in the chat.
